articles.title: Apple Watch users have access to an accessibility feature called AssistiveTouch
articles.summary: This feature allows users to control their device without touching the screen by detecting subtle movements made while holding the arm or hand still.
articles.content: Apple Watch users have a hidden feature at their disposal that allows them to control their device without touching the screen. This is made possible by AssistiveTouch, an accessibility feature designed for people with motor disabilities. However, it can also be used by anyone who wants to explore alternative ways of interacting with their watch. The Apple Watch interface is generally easy to use, relying on taps and rotations of the Digital Crown to navigate through menus and apps. But with AssistiveTouch enabled, users can control their device using subtle movements of their arm, hand, and fingers. This feature uses data from built-in sensors like the gyroscope, accelerometer, and optical heart rate sensor. Apple Watch owners who have upgraded to the latest version of watchOS already have some basic finger gestures available. For example, pinching your fingers twice allows you to interact with the screen. AssistiveTouch takes this concept further by detecting even the slightest movements made while holding the arm or hand still. With AssistiveTouch enabled, users can perform various tasks without touching their Apple Watch's screen. This includes tapping buttons, scrolling through menus, and even using Apple Pay for transactions. The feature relies on the built-in sensors to accurately detect these subtle movements. This unique feature is part of a suite of tools designed to enhance accessibility on the Apple Watch. While AssistiveTouch was initially created to help users with motor disabilities navigate their device, it can now be used by anyone who wants to explore alternative ways of interacting with their watch. To access AssistiveTouch on your Apple Watch, navigate to the Settings app and select Accessibility from the menu. From there, choose AssistiveTouch and flip the toggle switch to enable it. You'll also need to turn on Hand Gestures, which allows you to interact with your watch without physically touching the screen. Once AssistiveTouch is enabled, you can customize the actions assigned to each gesture. For example, a single tap with your fingers can be set to simulate a touch on the screen, while a double tap can open the Notification Center. This level of customization makes it possible for users to tailor AssistiveTouch to their specific needs. In addition to customizing gestures, you can also access tutorials and animations that demonstrate how to use AssistiveTouch effectively. Tap the "Try it out" text in the Hand Gestures settings to learn more about using these gestures in a guided environment. This interactive tutorial provides a clear understanding of how each gesture works. AssistiveTouch also includes other features, such as Motion Pointer, which places a cursor on your Apple Watch screen that you can control with the movement of your arm. This feature allows for precise navigation and selection on the watch's screen. When using AssistiveTouch, elements on the screen are highlighted to indicate which one will be tapped when making a specific gesture. Four default gestures handle navigation, so users can easily explore their Apple Watch without physically interacting with it. Enabling AssistiveTouch on your Apple Watch allows you to interact with the device without physically tapping the screen, making it a valuable feature for individuals with limited finger dexterity or mobility. This accessibility feature is particularly useful in everyday situations where hands are occupied, such as when cooking or carrying groceries, and also when wearing gloves that prevent precise touch interactions. AssistiveTouch can be set up quickly and easily on Apple Watch, but it's worth noting that doing so disables the universal double tap gesture for answering calls or scrolling through widgets. In addition to AssistiveTouch, there are other accessibility settings available on Apple devices that can enhance usability. For example, Auto-Answer Calls allows users to automatically answer incoming calls without needing to physically interact with their device, while Show Audio Transcriptions enables transcripts of HomePod announcements and Workout Buddy audio. These features, along with others like Reduce Transparency and adjustable Text Size, can be accessed through the accessibility settings on Apple devices, providing a range of options for users to customize their experience and improve usability. articles.title: iPod Modding Community Continues to Thrive Despite Device's Discontinuation
articles.summary: A London-based studio is working on a crowdsourced project called Sprout Pi Mainboard, which aims to modernize older iPod models by adding features like Bluetooth and Wi-Fi connectivity.
articles.content: The once beloved iPod has been out of production for years, but its legacy lives on through a thriving community of modders and enthusiasts who continue to breathe life into these devices. In October 2026, the iPod celebrated its 25th anniversary, although Apple chose not to publicly commemorate the occasion. However, the company did hide an interactive virtual iPod on the Apple Music website's error page, giving fans a nod to their beloved music player. A London-based studio has been working on a crowdsourced project that aims to modernize older iPod models by adding features like Bluetooth and Wi-Fi connectivity. This ambitious undertaking is dubbed Sprout Pi Mainboard, which essentially replaces the outdated logic board of older iPods with a new one. The project's YouTube launch video has garnered over 1 million views, demonstrating the enduring popularity of the iPod among nostalgic fans. For those who still cherish the memories of their trusty music player, this news is certainly exciting. This innovative approach to modding takes it a step further than traditional upgrades, which typically involve swapping out the hard drive for faster flash storage and installing a larger battery while preserving the original design and features. The limitations of traditional iPod modding become apparent when you try to sync music or stream services like Spotify on an old device. The usual approach of swapping out the hard drive and battery still leaves you stuck with outdated software, making it difficult to access modern features. A more innovative solution is offered by the Sprout logic board, which not only replaces the old hardware but also brings a host of new features to the table. This includes Bluetooth connectivity, Wi-Fi capabilities, and even support for lossless audio through a high-fidelity digital-to-analog converter (DAC). The Sprout logic board's functionality extends beyond just local playback, with some versions offering Wi-Fi support for streaming apps and AirPlay compatibility. This opens up possibilities for users to access their music libraries from the cloud or stream services directly on their iPod. Specific models of older iPods are compatible with the Sprout logic board, including certain generations of the mini and standard iPods. However, other models such as the classic, nano, and original iPods with color screens are not supported at this time. The project's developers are still working on implementing Spotify support and USB-C functionality for older iPod models. Until these features are finalized, it's essential to approach this initiative with a healthy dose of skepticism. Making purchasing decisions based solely on promises can be problematic. Subscribers to the Crowd Supply campaign will need to wait patiently as the team continues to develop these features. Pricing details and a release date have yet to be announced, leaving potential buyers in limbo for now. Those interested in staying informed about project updates can sign up for notifications on the project page. For those planning to participate, it's crucial to note that you'll need to provide your own iPod for the upgrade process. This means purchasing a unit if you don't already have one, which could be costly depending on the model you choose. The cost of acquiring an older iPod model may outweigh any potential benefits. While some iPod models did offer Bluetooth and Wi-Fi connectivity, many are no longer capable of running streaming apps due to outdated iOS versions. For instance, the 7th-generation iPod touch can only be updated to iOS 15. For those eager to revive their old iPod experience, alternatives to purchasing a new device are available. Modifying classic iPod models is one such option, allowing enthusiasts to breathe new life into vintage devices. Buying a used iPod touch and syncing music to it is another viable route, enabling users to connect their AirPods for an updated listening experience, albeit not with the latest iOS features.
